newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil up from overnight lows.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil up from overnight lows.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps bounced back at midday Tuesday from overnight lows on strong regional and tight prompt supplies despite a big drop in crude and product prices in the west on Monday, market sources said.
January gas oil swaps traded this morning from a low of $31.67 to $31.77 a barrel, up from a late night traded low of $31.55, brokers said. January swap was last quoted at $31.70/$31.80, they said.
"The market is supported by strong demand from China where stocks are low," one trader said.
Also the absence of arbitrage cargoes due to scarce availability of prompt products and a tight freight market has kept prices in Singapore steady, traders said.
On Monday January gas oil on the International Petroleum Exchange lost a hefty $7.50 a tonne to close at $216.75 per tonne while January Brent was down 46 cents to close at $24.10 a barrel.
Traders said the market was also held up by news of an unexpected shutdown to a cracker at the Shell refinery in Singapore.
Shell said on Monday that the 10,000 tonne-a-day thermal gas oil unit which cracks heavy residual fuel into middle distillates and fuel oil was partially shutdown on December 7.
The unit which is currently operating at 50 percent of capacity is expected to be closed for one week due to a leak in the furnace, Shell said.
The jet fuel market also edged down in line with the falls to gas oil prices but the jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade remained steady.
Janaury regrade was last quoted $1.55/$1.75 a barrel in thin trading, brokers said.
Fuel oil lost some ground in line with the weaker crude values in dull trading, with Janaury swaps last quoted at $118.25/$119.00 per tonne from Monday's $120.00/$120.50, brokers said.

Buyers were sidelined in the naphtha market due to the big falls to crude values with only sellers seen in the morning. January swaps was offered at $25.05 compared to Monday's bid price of $25.15, one broker said.
